Here’s how you can get that ID and then retrieve the details: | Step | What to do | Why it matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Locate the case ID** | • If you already have a docket number, case number, or any official identifier (e.g., “R‑12345” or “Adams‑2023‑01”), that is usually the ID.
• If you only know the parties’ names, use the internal search tool (or the public portal) to look up “R vs Adams.” The search results will list the case along with its ID. | The function can’t find a case unless you give it the exact ID. | | **2. Call the function** | Use the following JSON payload (replace `` with the real ID you found):
```json\n{\n \"case_id\": \"\",\n \"details\": true\n}\n```
Send this to the `legal_case_fetch` function. | `details:true` tells the system to return the full case record (judgment text, filings, docket entries, etc.). | | **4. Handle the response** | The function will return a structured object (JSON) containing:
• Case metadata (court, docket number, parties, dates)
• Full text of the opinion
• Links to related filings
• Citation information
• Any available annotations or summaries. | You can then parse, display, or store the data as needed. | ### Quick Example If the case ID turns out to be `RvsAdams-2024-NY`, you would call: ```python response = legal_case_fetch({ "case_id": "RvsAdams-2024-NY", "details": True }) print(response) ``` The `response` will contain all the detailed information you requested. --- #### Need help finding the ID?
